hero.headline: White House negotiates federal preemption of state AI regulations
hero.teaser: The White House is working with Capitol Hill to secure federal authority over some state AI regulations in exchange for technology policies on child safety and deepfakes.
hero.body:
The White House is negotiating with Capitol Hill to secure federal preemption of some state regulations on artificial intelligence in exchange for technology policies related to kids safety and deepfake protections. Sen. Marsha Blackburn is spearheading the negotiations with the White House to finalize text for an AI preemption package, according to the senator's spokesperson.

The negotiations represent an effort to establish a unified federal framework for AI regulation while addressing concerns that have emerged at the state level. The potential agreement would trade federal oversight for specific protections aimed at children and addressing manipulated media content.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal could be reached within days
cards.teaser: President Trump said a peace deal with Iran could be reached within two or three days.
cards.body:
President Trump told reporters in New York that a peace deal with Iran could be reached within two or three days. He made the comments after attending Game 3 of the NBA Finals.

The statement reflects ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations amid escalating tensions between the two countries. Any agreement would need to address the current conflict and could significantly affect energy markets and stability in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon as U.S.-Iran Peace Talks Stall
cards.body:
Israel launched extensive strikes in southern Lebanon this week, escalating military operations against Hezbollah even as diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran show signs of breakdown. The timing underscores the difficulty of achieving a regional ceasefire while military campaigns continue.

The Israeli military said it had struck 550 targets since the beginning of the week, a significant increase in tempo. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said his military is "deepening its operation" in Lebanon, with troops clashing with Hezbollah fighters along a strategic river in southern Lebanon as Israeli forces pushed farther north. Hezbollah confirmed point-blank combat with Israeli forces in a strategic town just beyond an Israeli-declared "yellow line" in the country's south.

The escalation comes amid a broader deterioration in U.S.-Iran negotiations. While Iran and the United States appeared to step back from direct military confrontation earlier in the week, new strikes and inflammatory rhetoric suggest those hopes may be premature. U.S. forces shot down four Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz and struck a ground control station in Iran's Bandar Abbas. Iran responded with a retaliatory attack on an American base in Kuwait, according to Iranian state media.

President Trump said Iran wants to make a deal but that the United States is "not satisfied" with current terms. "Either that or we'll have to just finish the job," Trump said at a cabinet meeting. He also made pointed remarks about Oman, a U.S. ally, saying the strait would be "open to everybody" and "Oman will behave just like everybody else or we'll have to blow them up." The White House did not immediately clarify the statement.

A major unresolved issue in talks is whether a U.S.-Iran ceasefire will cover Israel's operations against Hezbollah. Iran has insisted that Lebanon must be included in any agreement, while Israel has shown no willingness to halt military action against what it considers an immediate security threat on its northern border.

The humanitarian toll in Lebanon continues to mount. More than 1.2 million Lebanese have been displaced by Israeli strikes and evacuation orders since March, according to Lebanon's health ministry. Israeli strikes have killed more than 3,200 people. The ceasefire announced on April 16 appears close to collapse, with the World Health Organization reporting at least 608 people killed in Lebanon since the truce took effect.

Israeli military officials said 10 of its soldiers had been killed since the ceasefire began, with six killed by Hezbollah's explosive drones. Israel issued further evacuation warnings for residents of Tyre in Lebanon's south as operations continued.

cards.headline: U.S. Missile Strikes Sanctioned Oil Tanker Off Oman
cards.teaser: A crew issued a distress call after their vessel was hit by a missile fired from an American fighter jet.
cards.body:
A U.S. fighter jet fired a missile at a sanctioned oil tanker off the coast of Oman. The crew issued a distress call following the strike, requesting assistance.

All crew members were rescued after the incident occurred in waters near Oman.

cards.headline: House to vote on Republican immigration funding bill
cards.teaser: Congress is moving toward approval of $70 billion in funding for immigration enforcement agencies through the end of the current presidential term.
cards.body:
The House is set to vote on a Republican bill that would provide $70 billion to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection. The funding would extend through the remainder of the current administration.

The Senate has already approved the $70 billion allocation for the immigration agencies. The measure represents a significant increase in resources for federal immigration enforcement operations and border security efforts.

cards.headline: House Democrats oppose FISA extension without changes
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he will not vote to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act unless changes are made.
cards.body:
House Democratic leaders addressed reporters as their GOP counterparts seek to pass an extension of the nation's warrantless spying powers ahead of a June 12 deadline. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will not vote to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act unless acting Director makes specific changes.

The Section 702 program allows intelligence agencies to conduct surveillance without warrants under certain circumstances. The upcoming deadline has created urgency in Congress to either renew the program or allow it to expire, with Democratic leaders seeking reforms before supporting an extension.

cards.headline: Senate Majority Leader Thune seeks DNI nominee from White House
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader is pushing for the administration to put forward a Director of National Intelligence nominee soon.
cards.body:
Senate Majority Leader Thune has called for the White House to nominate a Director of National Intelligence soon. The request comes as the position requires Senate confirmation and plays a central role in coordinating the nation's intelligence agencies.

The Director of National Intelligence serves as the principal adviser to the president on intelligence matters and oversees the intelligence community. The timing of Thune's request suggests urgency in filling the position as the administration deals with national security matters including ongoing negotiations with Iran.

cards.headline: Drones from Russia-Ukraine War Stray into Neighboring Countries
cards.teaser: Unmanned aircraft launched by both Russia and Ukraine are veering off course and entering countries not involved in the war.
cards.body:
Unmanned aircraft launched by both Russia and Ukraine during their conflict are veering off course into neighboring countries. These drones have endangered civilians in nations uninvolved in the war, prompting residents to seek shelter when the aircraft appear.

The incidents underscore how modern warfare with unmanned systems extends beyond combat zones, affecting neutral populations through malfunctioning or misdirected weapons.

cards.headline: U.S. Missile Strikes Sanctioned Oil Tanker Off Oman
cards.teaser: A crew issued a distress call after their vessel was hit by a missile fired from an American fighter jet.
cards.body:
A U.S. fighter jet fired a missile at a sanctioned oil tanker off the coast of Oman. The crew issued a distress call following the strike, requesting assistance.

All crew members were rescued after the incident occurred in waters near Oman.

cards.headline: Man Arrested After Stabbing in Belfast
cards.teaser: Police arrested a Sudanese suspect in his 30s following an assault that was recorded and spread online.
cards.body:
A man in his 30s from Sudan was arrested in connection with a stabbing in Belfast, police said Tuesday. The suspect is alleged to have attacked another man in an assault that was recorded on video and quickly circulated on social media.

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer called for calm following the incident. Police are scheduled to provide an update on the case, and authorities have expressed concern that planned protests in response to the attack could lead to disorder. Northern Ireland leaders issued a joint statement condemning the violence.

cards.headline: Sea Drone Rescues U.S. Army Helicopter Crew Near Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: An uncrewed vessel picked up two crew members after their Apache helicopter went down on Monday.
cards.body:
An unmanned sea vessel rescued two crew members from a U.S. Army Apache helicopter that crashed near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The uncrewed vessel's successful recovery of the pilots marked an unusual application of autonomous maritime technology in a military emergency.

President Trump confirmed that both crew members were safe following the incident. The Strait of Hormuz remains a strategically important waterway where U.S. military forces maintain a regular presence.

cards.headline: Somali Referee Says U.S. Denied Him Entry for World Cup
cards.teaser: Omar Abdulkadir Artan said he had the proper documentation but was turned back, dashing his dream of becoming the first Somali to referee a World Cup match.
cards.body:
Omar Abdulkadir Artan was turned away at the U.S. border despite having all required documentation in order. The Somali referee said he possessed the proper papers needed for entry to the country.

Had he been allowed in, Artan would have made history as the first Somali national to officiate a World Cup match. He described the opportunity as a lifelong ambition that he was unable to fulfill.

cards.headline: Japanese City Captures Bear After Days of Sightings
cards.teaser: A black bear that prompted the closure of 94 schools and caused widespread fear was caught north of Tokyo.
cards.body:
Authorities in Utsunomiya, a city of half a million people about 100 kilometers north of Tokyo, successfully captured a black bear that had sparked unprecedented concern in the urban area. The medium-sized bear, estimated at about one meter long, was first spotted near a park on Saturday before being seen again on Sunday running past two young men in the city centre.

Officials closed all 94 primary and secondary schools as a precautionary measure following the sightings. The bear's appearance marked the first time such an animal had been seen in the municipality, prompting police and hunters to conduct an extensive search to remove the animal from populated areas.

hero.headline: US Army helicopter crew rescued after crash near Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
Two crew members of a US Army Apache helicopter were rescued after their aircraft went down near the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman. An uncrewed sea drone recovered both pilots following the crash on Monday, according to US officials who confirmed the details to CBS News.

The Apache is a twin-engine attack helicopter used primarily for close air support and reconnaissance operations. The exact cause of the crash has not been disclosed by military authorities.

The incident occurred in a strategically important region where global shipping and military operations intersect. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical passage for international oil transportation, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow waterway between Oman and Iran. US forces regularly operate in the area to maintain freedom of navigation and protect commercial shipping lanes.

The successful rescue highlights the growing role of autonomous maritime technology in military operations. The US military has deployed uncrewed surface vessels in the Persian Gulf region to enhance surveillance and emergency response capabilities. This incident demonstrates how these systems can be deployed effectively during crisis situations in remote locations.

The helicopter rescue comes amid heightened military activity and tensions in the region. Earlier in the week, a US fighter jet fired a missile that struck a sanctioned oil tanker near Oman. The tanker's crew issued a distress call requesting assistance after being hit and were subsequently rescued. The proximity of these two incidents underscores the complex security environment in the waters around the Strait of Hormuz, where commercial shipping, military operations, and geopolitical tensions frequently overlap.

President Trump indicated that the two helicopter crew members were in good condition following their rescue. He also expressed optimism regarding ongoing negotiations with Iran, suggesting that diplomatic discussions may be progressing in the region.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world's most strategically vital maritime chokepoints. Experts have raised concerns about potential closures or disruptions to the waterway, warning that such actions could set dangerous precedents for international shipping lanes and global trade. The region's importance to global energy supplies makes any incident affecting navigation particularly significant.

The deployment of autonomous vessels to assist in rescue operations represents an evolution in how military forces respond to emergencies in challenging environments. The successful recovery of the Apache crew demonstrates the practical value of these systems and their ability to operate in areas where traditional rescue methods might be limited. As military operations in the Persian Gulf continue, such technology may play an increasingly important role in protecting personnel and ensuring operational safety in this critical region.

cards.headline: Crew rescued after US missile strikes oil tanker off Oman
cards.teaser: The crew of a sanctioned oil tanker issued a distress call after a missile fired from a US fighter jet struck their vessel.
cards.body:
A sanctioned oil tanker was hit by a missile fired from a US fighter jet off the coast of Oman. The crew issued a distress call requesting immediate assistance following the strike.

All crew members were successfully rescued from the vessel in waters near Oman.

cards.headline: House to vote on Republican immigration funding bill
cards.teaser: Congress is moving toward approval of $70 billion in funding for immigration enforcement agencies through the end of the current presidential term.
cards.body:
The House is set to vote on a Republican bill that would provide $70 billion to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection. The funding would extend through the remainder of the current administration.

The Senate has already approved the $70 billion allocation for the immigration agencies. The measure represents a significant increase in resources for federal immigration enforcement operations and border security efforts.

cards.headline: Man sentenced in first sex-based harassment prosecution
cards.teaser: David Stroud was convicted in a prosecution that marked the first of its kind under sex-based harassment laws.
cards.body:
David Stroud was convicted in May in what prosecutors described as the first sex-based harassment prosecution of its type. During the incident that led to charges, Stroud grabbed a woman's hair and asked her for a kiss.

The conviction established new legal ground by demonstrating how harassment cases could be prosecuted under existing statutes. The case served as a test of legal provisions that had not previously been applied in this manner.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats vote as Platner controversies continue
cards.teaser: Graham Platner faces ongoing scrutiny over past conduct as Maine holds its Democratic Senate primary election.
cards.body:
Maine is holding its Democratic Senate primary as questions persist about candidate Graham Platner's background. Multiple news outlets have reported on controversies surrounding Platner's past that have emerged during the campaign.

Representative Ro Khanna has publicly defended Platner despite the scrutiny. Other Democrats, including opinion writers, have argued that Platner's history should disqualify him from Senate consideration. The primary results will determine which candidate advances to the general election.

cards.headline: Man jailed for killing partner and setting fire to London home
cards.teaser: Clifton George stabbed Annabel Rook 31 times before starting a fire at their house in north London.
cards.body:
Clifton George was sentenced to prison for murdering his partner Annabel Rook at their residence in north London. George stabbed Rook 31 times during the attack.

After the killing, George started a fire at the house. He was convicted of murder and arson following the incident.

cards.headline: Football regulator contacts West Ham over allegations against club owner
cards.teaser: Multiple women have accused billionaire David Sullivan of abuse of power and predatory behavior, including incidents when some were in their late teens.
cards.body:
The football regulator has contacted West Ham United following serious allegations against owner David Sullivan. Multiple women have accused the 77-year-old billionaire of sexual misconduct, including abusing his position of power and preying on them for sex. Some of the alleged incidents occurred when the women were in their late teens.

Sullivan, a former pornography businessman who owns 38.8% of the club, resigned as a director and co-chair on Saturday. A joint investigation by the BBC and the Times reported accounts from seven women. The football regulator may have the power to force Sullivan to sell his stake in the club as part of its inquiry.

hero.headline: Oil Prices Fall After Israel and Iran Agree to Halt Strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices declined after Israel and Iran announced they had stopped launching attacks against each other, easing concerns about a wider regional conflict that had pushed crude higher in recent days. The agreement temporarily reduces tensions in the Persian Gulf, a vital shipping corridor for global oil supplies.

The halt in military exchanges brought immediate relief to energy markets, which had been trading on heightened uncertainty. Crude oil futures fell as traders reassessed the risk of supply disruptions in the region. The Persian Gulf accounts for a substantial portion of global oil production and transport, making any conflict there a significant concern for energy markets worldwide.

The announcement came after a period of escalating military strikes between the two nations. Iran launched ballistic missile attacks on Israel, and Israeli warplanes responded with retaliatory strikes on Iran, marking the most direct confrontation since an April ceasefire. The escalation had prompted oil prices to spike as market participants factored in the possibility of disrupted shipping lanes or damaged energy infrastructure. The conflict also involved Yemen-based Houthi rebels aligned with Iran, who fired at Israel and warned they would target Israeli-affiliated ships in the Red Sea.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, acknowledged the halt in fighting in a televised speech but vowed to respond "with force" to future attacks. "At present, the fire on this front has been halted, because after the terrorist regime in Tehran was struck, it stopped attacking us," he said. "If that terrorist regime makes the mistake of attacking us again, we will respond with force."

Energy analysts noted that while the halt in strikes reduces immediate supply concerns, the underlying tensions remain unresolved. The agreement represents a pause rather than a comprehensive resolution to the longstanding disputes between the two nations. According to analysts, the ceasefire is fragile, with multiple flashpoints that could trigger fresh exchanges of strikes at any moment.

Israel has rejected Iranian efforts to link any definitive ceasefire to Israel stopping its military operations in Lebanon against Hezbollah, which has close ties with Tehran. Israel's defence minister stated that Israel would continue operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon and strike Beirut if the militant group attacked Israel.

Iran remained defiant, with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker, saying Tehran would not tolerate what it called "repeated violation." He stated that Iran's response would remain unchanged without a genuine willingness to build trust.

The impact of the reduced tensions extended beyond energy markets. Stock markets showed gains as investors grew more confident about regional stability. The easing of oil prices offers potential relief for consumers and businesses dealing with energy costs, though analysts caution that the geopolitical landscape in the region remains fragile and could shift quickly if hostilities resume.

cards.headline: U.S. Exports Grew in April as War Increased Oil Demand
cards.teaser: Commerce Department data showed American exports rose in April, slightly outpacing import growth.
cards.body:
U.S. exports increased in April, driven in part by higher demand for oil as the conflict with Iran affected global energy markets. Commerce Department data showed that exports grew at a slightly faster pace than imports during the month.

The war with Iran contributed to elevated oil prices and increased international demand for American energy products. The export growth reflects broader trade patterns influenced by the ongoing military conflict in the Persian Gulf region.

cards.headline: Pentagon Names Alibaba and Baidu Among Chinese Companies Aiding Military
cards.teaser: The Defense Department expanded its list of Chinese technology firms it says assist Beijing's military operations.
cards.body:
The Pentagon added Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD to its list of Chinese companies believed to be supporting Beijing's military efforts. The updated list was released Monday and supersedes a version from early 2025, marking a significant expansion of firms targeted by U.S. authorities.

The designations could escalate U.S.-China tensions and restrict these companies' access to American defense contracts and capital markets. The move comes less than a month after President Trump visited Beijing and met with Xi Jinping to maintain a trade war truce between the two nations.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise as Chip Stocks Rebound and Oil Retreats
cards.teaser: Major U.S. stock indexes gained as chipmakers rallied and oil prices declined following Middle East developments.
cards.body:
Semiconductor companies extended their recovery, with chipmakers posting their best two-day performance in a month. The gains helped drive broader market advances as investors rotated back into technology stocks following the recent sell-off.

Oil prices declined after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The reduction in regional conflict concerns boosted investor sentiment across equity markets.

cards.headline: OpenAI Prepares for Large IPO Amid Wave of AI Company Listings
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company is testing market appetite for its stock offering alongside planned IPOs from SpaceX and Anthropic.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially for an initial public offering, following rival Anthropic's IPO filing by about a week. The move intensifies the competition between the two leading artificial intelligence companies to go public.

The timing of multiple large technology IPOs—including OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX—has raised questions about whether financial markets can absorb such substantial stock offerings simultaneously. Analysts are examining whether investor demand for new technology stocks can support the combined scale of these planned listings.

cards.headline: Dubai Economy Faces Strain as Conflict Disrupts Trade and Travel
cards.teaser: The Persian Gulf conflict has exposed Dubai's economic vulnerability to disruptions in trade and tourism.
cards.body:
Oil prices have eased following an agreement between Iran and Israel to halt strikes against each other. The de-escalation reduces fears of a broader regional conflict that had previously driven crude prices higher.

Dubai's position as a major regional logistics and trade hub makes it vulnerable to disruptions in shipping and air travel. The emirate's economy depends heavily on commerce and international business operations, leaving it exposed to the effects of regional tensions.

cards.headline: Apple Delays Siri AI Upgrade in Europe Over Regulatory Dispute
cards.teaser: A regulatory disagreement has indefinitely postponed the release of enhanced artificial intelligence features for Siri in European markets.
cards.body:
Apple has indefinitely delayed the European launch of its upgraded Siri AI, which integrates the company's artificial intelligence tool Apple Intelligence. The delay stems from an ongoing regulatory dispute with European authorities.

The enhanced Siri, which will function more like AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini rather than a traditional web-based search tool, is scheduled for a wide release in the fall across other markets. European users will not have access to the upgrade while Apple resolves regulatory concerns.

hero.headline: Apple partners with Google and Nvidia to power AI features
hero.body:
Apple has announced a partnership with Google and Nvidia to run some of its artificial intelligence models on their cloud infrastructure. The company revealed the arrangement at its Worldwide Developers Conference, explaining that certain AI features will operate on servers managed by these technology companies rather than exclusively on Apple's own hardware.

Apple emphasized that the partnership maintains user privacy despite processing data on external servers. According to the company, users will not have their information accessible to Google or Nvidia, even when AI models run on those companies' infrastructure. This arrangement represents a shift from Apple's traditional approach of handling most processing on its own devices and servers.

At the conference, Apple introduced the third generation of its foundation models. The company unveiled a major upgrade to Siri, its voice assistant, which will now integrate with Apple's artificial intelligence tool, rebranded as "Siri AI." The new version will function more like AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini, rather than as a simple question-and-answer tool. Siri AI will be widely released in the fall alongside iOS 27.

The announcement highlighted regulatory challenges facing the company. Apple said the upgraded Siri AI features will not be available in Europe, citing unspecified restrictions. Some observers noted that while the AI improvements are significant for Apple, they lag behind capabilities already offered by competitors.

The conference also included updates to the company's visual design language. Apple announced improvements to Liquid Glass, its interface styling, and added a transparency slider that gives users more control over the appearance of their devices. The company redesigned app icons for many iPhone applications as part of iOS 27.

Additional announcements at the event included the expansion of App Bundles, which now allows developers to partner with one another to create discounted subscription packages. This feature enables developers to offer bundle deals across multiple apps or services.

Apple also revealed new child safety features amid increased scrutiny over image-related issues. The company addressed widespread concerns about protection measures on its devices during a period when governments and regulators have intensified pressure on technology firms to implement safeguards.

The partnership with Google and Nvidia underscores Apple's effort to compete in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence market. While the company has historically maintained strict control over its computing infrastructure, this collaboration suggests a willingness to leverage external cloud resources to deliver more advanced AI capabilities to its users, provided privacy protections remain in place.

cards.headline: Lovable reaches $500 million in annualized revenue
cards.teaser: The software company reported one million new projects created on its platform each week.
cards.body:
Lovable has surpassed $500 million in annualized run-rate revenue, driven by users who are building businesses and replacing internal software on its platform. The software development company has experienced rapid growth as both business users and individual developers adopt its tools.

The platform is generating significant activity, with users creating one million new projects each week.

cards.headline: Rivian releases $60,000 R2 electric vehicle
cards.teaser: The company's second electric vehicle model targets a lower price point than its existing trucks.
cards.body:
Rivian's second electric vehicle, the 2027 R2, is priced under $60,000 and marks the company's push toward mainstream success. The R2 follows Rivian's initial lineup of premium trucks and SUVs, which garnered significant media attention and a devoted following.

The R2 represents a critical shift in strategy as Rivian expands beyond its high-end truck segment. Early reviews indicate the vehicle delivers an engaging driving experience and meets expectations after its development period.

cards.headline: Sandstone raises $30 million for AI legal software
cards.teaser: The company plans to use the funding to develop artificial intelligence tools for in-house legal teams.
cards.body:
Sandstone completed a $30 million Series A funding round led by Lightspeed Partners, with Sequoia also participating in the investment.

The company provides artificial intelligence software for in-house legal departments. Sandstone plans to use the funding to expand its product offerings and grow its customer base among corporate legal teams.

cards.headline: Apple launches subscription bundles for App Store developers
cards.teaser: Developers can now partner with each other to offer discounted packages of their applications.
cards.body:
Apple expanded its App Bundles feature to allow developers to create subscription packages together. The change lets developers partner with one another to offer discounted bundles of their apps.

The feature brings a subscription model similar to streaming services to the App Store. Developers can now package multiple apps together and offer them at a reduced rate compared to purchasing each app separately.

cards.headline: Former scooter company founder raises $5 million for space data centers
cards.teaser: Euwyn Poon, who built 250,000 scooters at Spin, launched Orbital to deploy data centers in space.
cards.body:
Euwyn Poon, who previously founded Spin and oversaw production of 250,000 electric scooters, has raised $5 million for Orbital. The startup plans to deploy data centers in space rather than on the ground.

Orbital's ambitious goal is to launch 10,000 space-based data centers for processing and storage, marking a significant shift in Poon's focus from ground-based transportation infrastructure to orbital technology.

cards.headline: App Store adds personalized recommendations
cards.teaser: Apple will suggest applications based on user download history and behavior patterns.
cards.body:
Apple introduced personalized app recommendations to the App Store. The feature suggests applications based on what users have previously downloaded and how they use their devices.

The recommendation system analyzes user behavior to surface relevant apps. Apple joins other platforms that have long offered personalized content suggestions based on usage patterns.

hero.headline: Brewers Defeat Athletics 29-9 in High-Scoring Las Vegas Opener
hero.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Oakland Athletics 29-9 in a wild game marking the start of the Athletics' homestand in Las Vegas. The two teams combined for 11 home runs in what became one of the highest-scoring games of the season.

The contest took place as the Athletics returned to Las Vegas, where they had played 30 years ago. The game featured an offensive explosion from both sides, with the Brewers ultimately pulling away despite the Athletics hitting six home runs of their own.

The 29 runs scored by Milwaukee represented a season high for the team. The Athletics' six home runs were not enough to keep pace with the Brewers' offensive output in a game where pitching struggled on both sides.

The game served as the opening contest of the Athletics' current homestand in Las Vegas. The Athletics had been away from the city for three decades before this series began.

The final score of 29-9 made this one of the most lopsided high-scoring games of the season. Both teams will look to recalibrate their pitching staffs after the offensive showcase that saw 38 total runs scored between the two clubs.

cards.headline: Joel Bitonio Retires After 12 Seasons With Browns
cards.teaser: Seven-time Pro Bowl guard Joel Bitonio announced his retirement from the NFL after spending his entire career with Cleveland.
cards.body:
Joel Bitonio announced his retirement after 12 seasons with the Cleveland Browns. The guard was selected to seven Pro Bowls during his career, all spent with Cleveland.

Bitonio played his entire NFL career with the Browns organization. He was considered a potential offseason target for the Detroit Lions before making his retirement decision.

cards.headline: South Carolina Set to Hire Kevin Schnall as Baseball Coach
cards.teaser: South Carolina is expected to hire Coastal Carolina's Kevin Schnall as its next head baseball coach.
cards.body:
South Carolina is set to hire Kevin Schnall as its next head baseball coach. Schnall currently serves as head coach at Coastal Carolina.

The hire comes as South Carolina conducts its coaching search.

---

Note: The additional source material provided is about unrelated stories (Crystal Palace soccer coaching and Trump at the NBA Finals) and does not contain information about the South Carolina baseball coaching hire. The card text has been retained as originally written since no relevant source material was available to expand or verify the details.

cards.headline: Emma Raducanu Wins Opening Match at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Emma Raducanu defeated Anna Blinkova in straight sets at Queen's Club to begin her Wimbledon preparations.
cards.body:
Emma Raducanu, Britain's top-ranked player, made a dominant start to her grass-court season at Queen's Club, defeating Russia's Anna Blinkova 6-0 6-3 to reach the second round.

The commanding straight-set victory demonstrates Raducanu's readiness as she prepares for Wimbledon later this month.

cards.headline: Miles Russell Qualifies for US Open With Charlie Woods Caddying
cards.teaser: 17-year-old Miles Russell qualified for the US Open with Tiger Woods' son Charlie serving as his caddie.
cards.body:
Miles Russell, 17, qualified for the US Open after winning a 36-hole qualifier in Florida on Monday. The world's No. 10 amateur secured the fourth and final spot available, surviving a playoff to earn his place in the tournament at Shinnecock Hills.

Charlie Woods, son of three-time US Open champion Tiger Woods, caddied for Russell during the qualifying round. The two are close friends who share the same commercial agent and will both attend Florida State University to play college golf.

cards.headline: Linsey Smith Becomes Top-Ranked T20 Bowler
cards.teaser: England's Linsey Smith has risen to become the number one T20 bowler in the world after a difficult start to her international career.
cards.body:
Linsey Smith has reached the number one ranking among T20 bowlers in the world. The England player admitted to struggling during the first part of her international career, saying she hated that early period.

Smith has transformed her fortunes since those initial difficulties. She now holds the top ranking in T20 bowling, representing a significant turnaround from her self-described period of self-doubt.

cards.headline: Somali Referee Omar Artan Denied Entry to United States for World Cup
cards.teaser: Referee Omar Artan says he was barred from entering the US despite having proper documentation for the World Cup.
cards.body:
Somali referee Omar Artan has been denied entry to the United States and will miss the 2026 World Cup, where he was set to become the first official from Somalia to officiate at the tournament. Despite holding what he described as proper documentation and visa, Artan was turned away after an 11-hour immigration interview.

FIFA confirmed Artan's exclusion, stating that U.S. authorities informed the organization that his status would not change. The denial reflects broader visa complications affecting the tournament as FIFA navigates the Trump administration's stricter border policies—a challenge the organization avoided in previous World Cups through special arrangements in host countries.

hero.headline: Spielberg Returns to Summer Blockbuster Season With Disclosure Day
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg is returning to the summer movie season with his new film Disclosure Day, aiming to reclaim his title as the king of the summer box office. The director helped establish the summer blockbuster model with Jaws, which opened in June 1975 and demonstrated the financial potential of releasing major films during the school vacation period.

More than 50 years have passed since Jaws terrified audiences and changed Hollywood's approach to summer releases. Spielberg was 28 years old when that film premiered, launching a career that would define blockbuster filmmaking for generations.

The new film represents Spielberg's latest attempt to prove he can still draw massive audiences during the competitive summer season. Disclosure Day arrives at a time when the theatrical landscape has shifted significantly from the era when Jaws first made its impact, with streaming services and changing audience habits presenting new challenges for traditional cinema releases.

Spielberg's track record with summer releases extends far beyond Jaws. His films have consistently performed well during the season, helping cement his reputation as one of Hollywood's most commercially successful directors. The summer blockbuster model he helped pioneer has become a cornerstone of the film industry's annual calendar, with studios now planning their biggest releases around the period when audiences have more free time to visit theaters.

Disclosure Day will test whether Spielberg's name and filmmaking approach can still compete in a crowded marketplace where superhero franchises and established intellectual property often dominate the box office charts. The film's performance will be watched closely by industry observers as a measure of whether traditional auteur-driven blockbusters can still achieve the kind of cultural and commercial impact that defined earlier decades of summer moviegoing.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Scores 22nd Top 10 Album Since Beatles Split
cards.teaser: The former Beatle's latest release The Boys of Dungeon Lane reaches the top 10 on the Billboard 200 chart.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney has secured his 22nd top 10 hit on the Billboard 200 chart since the Beatles disbanded. The milestone comes with his latest album The Boys of Dungeon Lane, which has climbed into the upper reaches of the weekly album rankings.

The chart performance extends McCartney's decades-long success as a solo artist following the breakup of the Beatles. His consistent ability to land albums in the top 10 demonstrates sustained commercial appeal spanning more than five decades of recording and releasing new music.

cards.headline: Netflix Renews A Good Girls Guide to Murder for Final Season
cards.teaser: The mystery series starring Emma Myers will conclude with a third season adapting the final book in Holly Jackson's trilogy.
cards.body:
Netflix has renewed A Good Girls Guide to Murder for a third and final season. The series stars Emma Myers as Pip, an amateur sleuth investigating crimes in her community.

The upcoming season will complete the adaptation of Holly Jackson's bestselling book trilogy and bring Pip's investigation arc to its conclusion. The final installment will consist of four episodes, following the same format as previous seasons of the show.

cards.headline: Girl Meets World Producer Describes Difficult Table Read Incident
cards.teaser: Sabrina Carpenter and Rowan Blanchard cried during a table read after treatment by the show's creator, according to a new documentary.
cards.body:
A producer on Girl Meets World revealed that stars Sabrina Carpenter and Rowan Blanchard cried during a table read after being treated poorly by the show's creator. The disclosure appears in Doc Meets World, a documentary featuring cast members from Boy Meets World discussing their experiences on both the original series and its spinoff.

The documentary premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival and features Danielle Fishel, Will Friedle, and Rider Strong sharing candid accounts of their time working on the shows. The revelation about the difficult working conditions on Girl Meets World adds to a broader conversation about the experiences of young performers in the entertainment industry.

cards.headline: Director Sophia Takal Debuts Teen Actress Thriller at Tribeca
cards.teaser: Act One follows a young actress who enrolls in an acting class after being rejected by her school's drama club.
cards.body:
Sophia Takal's new film Act One premiered at the Tribeca Festival. The thriller stars Ella Beatty as Hannah, a teenage actress determined to achieve greatness in her craft.

The film explores Hannah's journey after she is rejected by her school's drama club and decides to pursue acting through an alternative path by enrolling in an acting class. Takal wrote and directed the film, which examines the lengths a young performer will go to succeed in the competitive world of acting.

cards.headline: Helena Zengel Meets Real Person She Portrays in Westend Girl
cards.teaser: The rising star discussed the emotional reaction when the subject of the German thriller series first watched footage.
cards.body:
Helena Zengel met the woman she portrays in Westend Girl, a German thriller series about the drug trade. When the real-life subject first watched clips from the show, she cried, according to Zengel.

The series premiered at Seriencamp and is being distributed worldwide by Beta Film. Zengel, who has gained international recognition for her acting work, stars in the production which is based on real events involving its subject.

cards.headline: The Simpsons Join Monopoly Go Mobile Game
cards.teaser: Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa and Maggie appear in what the developers call the game's biggest collaboration to date.
cards.body:
The Simpsons family has been integrated into Monopoly Go, the mobile game from Scopely. The collaboration launched last week and represents the largest partnership for the game, which has previously featured tie-ins with Marvel, Star Wars, and Harry Potter properties.

The integration marks the most adult-oriented collaboration for Monopoly Go so far. All five main Simpson family members appear in the game as part of a special in-game event for players.

hero.headline: White House negotiates federal preemption of state AI regulations
hero.teaser: The White House is working with Capitol Hill to secure federal authority over some state AI regulations in exchange for technology policies on child safety and deepfakes.
hero.body:
The White House is negotiating with Capitol Hill to secure federal preemption of some state regulations on artificial intelligence in exchange for technology policies related to kids safety and deepfake protections. Sen. Marsha Blackburn is spearheading the negotiations with the White House to finalize text for an AI preemption package, according to the senator's spokesperson.

The negotiations represent an effort to establish a unified federal framework for AI regulation while addressing concerns that have emerged at the state level. The potential agreement would trade federal oversight for specific protections aimed at children and addressing manipulated media content.

cards.headline: Trump approval rating remains at 35 percent amid Iran conflict
cards.teaser: A new Reuters/Ipsos poll shows President Trump's approval rating near the lowest point of his political career as Americans express concern about rising gasoline prices.
cards.body:
President Trump's approval rating stands at 35 percent, near the lowest level of his political career, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday. Americans surveyed said they expect gasoline prices to continue rising due to the Iran war.

The poll results reflect public sentiment as the administration navigates an active conflict with Iran. The low approval numbers come as Trump faces pressure on both foreign policy and domestic economic concerns, particularly regarding energy costs that directly affect American households.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal could be reached within days
cards.teaser: President Trump said a peace deal with Iran could be reached within two or three days.
cards.body:
President Trump told reporters in New York that a peace deal with Iran could be reached within two or three days. He made the comments after attending Game 3 of the NBA Finals.

The statement reflects ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations amid escalating tensions between the two countries. Any agreement would need to address the current conflict and could significantly affect energy markets and stability in the Middle East.

cards.headline: House Democrats oppose FISA extension without changes
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he will not vote to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act unless changes are made.
cards.body:
House Democratic leaders addressed reporters as their GOP counterparts seek to pass an extension of the nation's warrantless spying powers ahead of a June 12 deadline. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will not vote to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act unless acting Director makes specific changes.

The Section 702 program allows intelligence agencies to conduct surveillance without warrants under certain circumstances. The upcoming deadline has created urgency in Congress to either renew the program or allow it to expire, with Democratic leaders seeking reforms before supporting an extension.

cards.headline: Sam Bankman-Fried applies for presidential pardon
cards.teaser: The FTX founder, serving a 25-year sentence for fraud, has formally applied for a pardon after completion of his sentence.
cards.body:
FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried has formally applied for a presidential pardon while serving a 25-year sentence for fraud charges stemming from the cryptocurrency exchange's collapse. The application was officially submitted on Monday.

Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud related to FTX's high-profile failure, which caused substantial losses for investors and customers of the platform. His pardon application represents a formal step in seeking relief from his current sentence.

cards.headline: Senate Majority Leader Thune seeks DNI nominee from White House
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader is pushing for the administration to put forward a Director of National Intelligence nominee soon.
cards.body:
Senate Majority Leader Thune has called for the White House to nominate a Director of National Intelligence soon. The request comes as the position requires Senate confirmation and plays a central role in coordinating the nation's intelligence agencies.

The Director of National Intelligence serves as the principal adviser to the president on intelligence matters and oversees the intelligence community. The timing of Thune's request suggests urgency in filling the position as the administration deals with national security matters including ongoing negotiations with Iran.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from website and YouTube
cards.teaser: The Kennedy Center scrubbed references to President Trump from its website and YouTube pages, though his name remains on other social media accounts.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center on Monday scrubbed its website and YouTube pages of references to President Trump. Trump's name was also excluded from formal invitations to the annual honors ceremony at the center. However, his name remains on the venue's Instagram, Facebook and X accounts.

The move follows a court ruling, though the center has not provided detailed explanation for the selective removal across its digital platforms. The Kennedy Center, a national cultural institution in Washington, typically includes the sitting president in its formal communications and events.
